rationale: The literature supports that NFU1 variants cause a spectrum that frequently manifests as complex hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) with long-term evolution to include sensory-motor polyneuropathy, cognitive decline, and leukoencephalopathy. However, the defining study (Kaiyrzhanov et al., 2022) explicitly identifies 'early-onset pure' hereditary spastic paraplegia as an established presentation within the phenotypic continuum, and the provided sources do not provide exact cohort numerator and denominator data to verify that pure HSP occurs in fewer than 25% of affected individuals.

evidence.text: Kaiyrzhanov et al. (2022) identified that NFU1 missense variants are associated with a clinical continuum extending from early-onset pure HSP to complex hereditary spastic paraplegia, supporting broad neurodegenerative involvement but confirming pure HSP as part of the clinical spectrum.

source.title: Phenotypic continuum of NFU1‐related disorders
source.quote: NFU1 missense variants associated with a phenotype ranging from early-onset pure to complex hereditary spastic paraplegia

evidence.text: Tonduti et al. (2015) reported an NFU1-mutated patient presenting with slowly progressive spastic paraparesis with relapsing-remitting episodes, whose phenotype evolved over decades to include mild cognitive impairment and a mixed sensory-motor neuropathy in the third decade.

source.title: New spastic paraplegia phenotype associated to mutation of NFU1
source.quote: mild cognitive impairment and a long survival. The early white matter abnormalities observed on MRI was combined with a mixed sensory-motor neuropathy in the third decade.

numbers.metric: Affected individuals described in case report

evidence.text: Parodi et al. (2018) classified the phenotype associated with NFU1 mutations within the complicated spastic paraplegia and spastic-ataxia spectrum.

source.title: Hereditary ataxias and paraparesias: clinical and genetic update
source.quote: The related phenotype was complicated spastic paraplegia

evidence.text: Uzunhan et al. (2020) demonstrated intrafamilial variability in NFU1-related disease, with one sibling presenting with spastic paraparesis and cavitating leukodystrophy mimicking cerebral palsy while the other experienced early infantile lethality.

source.title: A genetic mimic of cerebral palsy: Homozygous NFU1 mutation with marked intrafamilial phenotypic variation
source.quote: showed clinical signs and symptoms of spastic paraparesis with a relapsing-remitting course... sister with a severe phenotype who died at the age of 16 months.

conflicts: Kaiyrzhanov et al. explicitly document 'early-onset pure' hereditary spastic paraplegia in the NFU1 spectrum, conflicting with assertions that pure HSP does not occur or is negligible.
The available literature snippets do not report the exact cohort denominator or breakdown necessary to quantitatively substantiate the '<25%' threshold for pure HSP.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact ratio of pure versus complex HSP presentations in the complete Kaiyrzhanov et al. (2022) cohort at initial presentation versus long-term follow-up?
new_directions.rationale: Extracting the full cohort numbers from Kaiyrzhanov et al. will formally test whether pure HSP accounts for under 25% of cases upon initial evaluation and how many convert to complex HSP over time.

new_directions.question_text: Does the specific NFU1 variant (e.g., p.Gly189Arg vs p.Val241Leu) correlate with pure spastic paraplegia versus fatal infantile mitochondrial encephalopathy?
new_directions.rationale: Genotype-phenotype mapping could explain why some missense variants cause slowly progressive spasticity whereas others cause fatal early-onset multiple mitochondrial dysfunctions syndrome.
